Five more Ukrainians return from occupied territories
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
02:29:00 UTC
11:29:00 KST

Five more Ukrainians return from occupied territories
The “Bring Kids Back UA” initiative reported this on Facebook, according to Ukrinform.
As part of the Ukrainian President’s “Bring Kids Back UA” initiative, the Helping to Leave team worked together to successfully return Natalia, Katya, and Maria (names changed for security reasons) to territory controlled by Ukraine.
Natalia and Katya are sisters from a large family. Their older brothers had left the temporarily occupied territory earlier, so the girls and their mother eventually decided to leave as well and turned to Helping to Leave for assistance. The team helped the family organize their route and accompanied them during their departure. With the assistance of the Coordination Headquarters, the sisters received permits to return to Ukraine and, together with their mother, successfully crossed the border.
Today, the family is in territory controlled by Ukraine and is reunited with their older brothers. The girls plan to continue their lives here.
Maria left a part of the Luhansk region occupied by Russia back in 2014. There, she managed to complete only one grade under the Ukrainian curriculum before being forced to study under the Russian one. Maria also reached out to Helping to Leave. The team helped plan her route, and with the assistance of the Coordination Headquarters, she received a return permit and was able to travel to territory controlled by Ukraine.
Maria is now back in Ukraine. She plans to finish 11th grade and then work and build her future here.
Also, as part of the President of Ukraine’s “Bring Kids Back UA” initiative, thanks to the efforts of the Compass of Dreams NGO team, two more young people were successfully returned to Ukrainian-controlled territory.
Eighteen-year-old Kyrylo (name changed for security reasons) had been living under occupation since 2014, when he was still a child. His family supported his desire to live and study in a free Ukraine. Therefore, even before reaching the age of majority, he enrolled remotely in a Ukrainian institution of higher education. The team at the “Compass of Dreams” NGO helped Kyrylo obtain the necessary documents and arranged his departure. Just one week after turning 18, he was able to leave the temporarily occupied territory and return to free Ukraine.
Seventeen-year-old Maria (name changed for security reasons) was still a child when Russia occupied her hometown in 2022. The occupiers quickly closed Ukrainian schools, but she refused to attend a Russian school and, despite the risks, secretly continued her Ukrainian education online. Maria and her parents were pressured to obtain Russian passports, but the family refused. The pressure intensified when Russian soldiers came to their home, ostensibly to “get to know them.” Despite this, Maria remotely earned a Ukrainian high school diploma and enrolled in college under Quota-2. The young woman reached out to the NGO “Compass of Dreams” for help several months before her departure. After careful preparation, Maria, along with her grandmother, was able to leave the temporarily occupied territory. She is now in Chernivtsi and will begin her freshman year and a new life in a free Ukraine this September.
As reported by Ukrinform, at the end of August, 23 Ukrainians returned home from the temporarily occupied territories—including elderly people, citizens with limited mobility, Ukrainians with health issues, and families with children.

Pacific summit backs concerns over China missile test despite Nauru dissent
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
02:21:36 UTC
11:21:36 KST

Pacific summit backs concerns over China missile test despite Nauru dissent
- Pacific Island leaders expressed concern over China’s July missile test, urging transparency and advance warnings for such tests in the region.
- Nauru dissented from the consensus, reflecting its recent diplomatic ties with China amid regional disagreements.
- China dismissed claims of threats, accusing Palau of exaggeration and opposing Taiwan’s participation in the summit, which caused tensions among members.
AI generated
SYDNEY – Pacific Island leaders expressed concern about China’s Pacific missile test at their annual summit, though Nauru formally dissented, in a meeting largely overshadowed by Beijing’s objections to Taiwan’s presence.
Summit host and Palau President Surangel Whipps Jr said on Sept 3 that China’s intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) test in July, Beijing’s first known launch in the Pacific since September 2024, passed over several island nations without adequate warning.
“Leaders called on all states undertaking ICBM testing to ensure transparency and reassurance, including through the provision of advance notification of a test at least 24 hours in accordance with international practice,” he said at a media briefing at the conclusion of the Pacific Islands Forum.
“I might note that the Republic of Nauru has dissented,” he added, reading from a prepared statement.
Nauru, which has a history of switching diplomatic recognition between Beijing and Taipei, re-established diplomatic ties with China in 2024.
China’s Foreign Ministry, in response to the statement, said the country is committed to peaceful development and pursues a defensive national defence policy, adding that it has never engaged in military expansion.
“China is willing to work with South Pacific countries to contribute to safeguarding peace, stability, development and prosperity in the region,” ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said at a regular press conference.
Australian Energy Minister Chris Bowen, who attended the summit with Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, said on Sept 4 it was “perfectly reasonable for the vast majority of Pacific countries to express a view and for one or two to say that they have a different view”.
“Unanimity is not necessary to express very strong views on behalf of the vast majority of the Pacific island states, which was very clear,” Bowen told ABC Radio.
Beijing accuses Palau of ‘hype’ over missile test
The consensus came after a meeting of the 18-member grouping’s foreign ministers in August failed to agree on a statement condemning the test, despite public and private expressions of concern from several leaders about the region’s militarisation.
Palau, one of three Pacific island nations that maintain official diplomatic ties with Taiwan, had pushed the group to formally condemn the missile test.
Beijing pushed back on Sept 3, accusing Palau of stirring “hype” over the missile test and warning that its attempts to influence fellow Pacific island nations were “malicious and will not succeed”.
The summit was further strained by China’s objections to Taiwan’s participation, with Beijing arguing the island was not qualified to attend. China claims democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory – a position Taiwan firmly rejects.
Proceedings were also overshadowed by the absence of five Pacific leaders, who sent low-ranking ministers in their place.
The next Pacific Islands Forum leaders’ summit will be hosted by New Zealand in 2027. REUTERS

Musk super PAC wades into US midterms with $800,000 for Republicans in close races
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
02:21:19 UTC
11:21:19 KST

Elon Musk’s super PAC wades into US midterms with more than $1m for Republicans in close races
NEW YORK – SpaceX founder Elon Musk has spent more than US$800,000 (S$1 million) in recent days on over a dozen key congressional races through his super Political Action Committee (PAC), funding direct-mail and other campaign materials for Republican candidates who face close races in the midterm elections.
Musk’s America PAC, which has been sitting on a US$50 million war chest funded by the world’s richest man, reported its first spending for the 2026 election in a filing late on Sept 2, with a focus on races in Texas and other battleground states.
The PAC expects to play a major role in Republican voter turnout efforts, with spending on door knockers, digital advertising and direct-mail campaigns ahead of the Nov 3 election, Reuters reported in July. It has a funding target of up to US$120 million, according to The New York Times.
A spokesperson for America PAC declined to comment on Sept 3. SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
The PAC spent the most money in Texas, where Musk’s SpaceX is headquartered with multiple rocket and Starlink facilities.
Texas Attorney-General Ken Paxton has received a US$247,595 boost from Musk since Aug 20 for his Senate race against Democrat James Talarico, who has been narrowly leading in public opinion polls since mid-April according to election tracker Nate Silver’s Silver Bulletin.
US Senator Susan Collins, a Maine Republican and the chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee which controls federal spending, was the next biggest beneficiary with US$170,224 going towards her campaign, the filing shows. She is in a closely watched race against Democrat Troy Jackson.
In Ohio, where Republican Senator Jon Husted faces a tough battle to keep his seat against former senator Sherrod Brown, America PAC has printed US$105,675 in materials.
Like Collins, Husted sits on the Senate Appropriations Committee which controls the funding for some of Musk’s biggest government contracts at SpaceX.
The PAC’s filing showed Musk also boosted the campaign of Senator Dan Sullivan, an Alaska Republican who sits on the Senate Armed Services Committee.
That committee oversees the Pentagon and many of the projects that Musk’s space, satellite and artificial intelligence companies provide to the federal government.
In US House races, Musk’s PAC boosted several sitting members of the Armed Services, Foreign Affairs and Homeland Security committees as well as other committees that may touch on or oversee the work of his companies.
They include Republican Representatives Scott Perry and Ryan Mackenzie of Pennsylvania, Tom Kean of New Jersey, Jennifer Kiggans of Virginia, Mike Lawler of New York and Derrick Van Orden of Wisconsin.
All of the spending disclosed on the night of Sept 2 was for “printing”, suggesting that it was used for direct-mail, postcards, door hangers, canvassing literature, yard signs and the like.
The spending has drawn criticism from Democrats, including US Representative Chris Pappas, who is favoured in polls to win next week’s Democratic primary for the New Hampshire Senate race.
If victorious, he would face former Republican Senator John Sununu, who is running for his old seat.
Musk’s PAC spent more than US$90,000 on materials opposing Pappas, who has been highly critical of Musk’s past work running the Department of Government Efficiency.
“MAGA Republicans like Elon Musk are trying to buy this Senate seat for John Sununu because they know he would be a rubber stamp for Donald Trump’s toxic agenda,” Rachel Petri, Pappas’ campaign manager, said in a statement to Reuters.
Sununu’s office did not return a request for comment.
A spokesman for US Representative Ryan Mackenzie said the campaign has not talked with any super PACs, including Musk’s, about coordinated campaign spending.
Spokesman Arnaud Armstrong said Mackenzie was a champion for government reform “leading the charge to crack down on congressional stock trading, taking on large corporations and holding big tech accountable”.
A spokesperson for Husted declined to comment while representatives for the other Republican candidates did not immediately return requests for comment. REUTERS

Israel Police: Terrorist neutralized after attempted stabbing in Jerusalem Old City
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
02:09:31 UTC
11:09:31 KST

Key Events
Updates
Palestinian reports: IDF launches raids in West Bank, fires live ammo, stun grenades
The Israeli military launched raids across the West Bank, Shehab and Quds News reported, saying the soldiers fired stun grenades and live ammunition in one of the raids.
According to the Palestinian outlets, the IDF raided the Arab American University dormitories in the Palestinian city of Jenin in the northern West Bank, also raiding Tammun and Wadi al-Far'a, both south of the Palestinian city of Tubas.
The IDF also reportedly raided the village of Beitin near Ramallah and Qalandiya refugee camp on the northern outskirts of Jerusalem, firing stun grenades and live ammunition. According to Quds News, the IDF also raided the village of al-Nazla al-Sharqiya, north of Tulkarm.
IDF launches strikes in Lebanon, cites attempted Hezbollah drone attack
The Israeli military said it began a wave of strikes in Lebanon after its soldiers downed a Hezbollah drone in the IDF-occupied buffer zone in southern Lebanon.
"Earlier today, terrorists from the Hezbollah terrorist organization launched a drone towards IDF soldiers operating in the Security Zone in southern Lebanon," it said, adding that the soldiers shot down the drone and suffered no injuries in the incident.
Earlier on Friday, Lebanon's Al Mayadeen channel reported that an Israeli drone strike killed two in Kfar Roummane, near the city of Nabatieh in southern Lebanon.
Strikes were also reported in the city's Nabatieh al-Fouqa suburb and in the nearby village of Kfour. According to Al Mayadeen, Israeli aircraft also bombed the village of Ain el-Tineh in the Bekaa Valley region in eastern Lebanon.

A bill to strengthen sanctions against Russia, which the U.S. Senate supported by an overwhelming majority last month, has faced opposition in the House of Representatives and may not be put to a vote before the midterm elections on November 3. Bloomberg reports, according to UNN.
Details
The document would allow President Donald Trump to impose 100% tariffs on the largest buyers of Russian oil and gas, as well as on countries that help Moscow circumvent energy sanctions. The main buyers of Russian energy resources include China, India, and Turkey.

Congress fears rising gasoline prices

Lawmakers are also assessing the risk of rising oil and gasoline prices if India and other buyers of Russian crude are forced to seek alternative suppliers.
The Senate previously approved the bill by a vote of 86 to 11, but the necessary support for its swift passage is not yet available in the House of Representatives.

'Winds of change' favour Argentina in Falklands row with UK — Milei

02:00:23 UTC
11:00:23 KST

President Javier Milei has said that the "winds of change" favoured Argentina's claim to the Falkland Islands, pointing to Washington's readiness to review its neutrality on his country's territorial dispute with Britain.
"There are winds of change in the world that are favourable to our claim," Milei said in a nationally televised address on Thursday about the South Atlantic archipelago, a British territory.
Britain and Argentina fought a war over the islands in 1982.
Control of the islands, referred to by Argentines as Las Malvinas, remains a highly emotive issue in Argentina and periodically leads to tensions with Britain.
Argentina players held up a banner saying "The Falklands are Argentine" after beating England 2-1 in the World Cup semi-final earlier this year.
The fate of the islands has hit headlines again in recent days, with US President Donald Trump threatening to wade into the dispute and a British-Israeli oil project near the islands causing anger in Argentina.
Push back
Flanked by cabinet members, Milei assured Argentina would not "stand idly by" and announced tougher sanctions on firms linked to Falklands oil projects.
On Tuesday, Argentine Falklands War veterans and environmental lawyers filed a lawsuit to halt the project promoted by the British company Rockhopper and the Israeli company Navitas in waters north of the islands.
Milei said the project violated a United Nations resolution calling on both sides to desist from unilateral actions in the Falklands while the dispute is ongoing.
"We will not allow it," he said.
"If we allow it, we will be creating an incentive for the British government to deepen the occupation of the islands and the exploitation of our resources."
His address comes as his approval ratings plummet, just over a year before he seeks re-election.
Polls show only around 34 percent of Argentines supporting his actions.
The Falkland Islands have a population of 3,000 to 3,600 people. In a 2013 referendum, over 90 percent voted in favour of remaining an overseas UK territory.

Milei vows tougher sanctions, defense push over Falklands oil drilling
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
01:56:28 UTC
10:56:28 KST

Argentina's Milei steps up Falklands sovereignty claims with oil sanctions
BUENOS AIRES/LONDON, Sept 3 - Argentine President Javier Milei said he would sanction oil companies drilling in the Falkland Islands, stepping up the country's claims to sovereignty over the British overseas territory.
Milei's comments in a televised national address on Thursday came days after U.S. President Donald Trump said he was reviewing the United States' neutral position on the remote archipelago in the South Atlantic.
The prospect of oil firms carrying out exploration in the islands, which Argentina calls Las Malvinas, was an urgent threat to Argentine interests, Milei said, 44 years after his country was defeated by Britain in a war over sovereignty.
Milei, a Trump ally, referenced the possible shift in the U.S. position and said "winds of change" favoured the Argentine claim. He said he was sending Congress a bill aimed at strengthening Argentina's response to violations of its sovereignty.
BRITISH POSITION 'UNWAVERING'
Britain, which has controlled the territory since 1833, said on Friday that its position on the islands was "unwavering".
"The Islands are British and will remain so because that is the overwhelming position of the Islanders," British foreign minister Ed Miliband said on X.
"Their right of self-determination is paramount, grounded in international law and we will resolutely uphold it."
British defence minister Wes Streeting added that Milei's words reflected "domestic politics in Argentina".
Milei had previously favoured diplomacy as the best way to pursue Argentina's claim to the Falklands, but with more oil drilling due in the coming months and Trump's repeated mention of the islands he is now striking a tougher tone.
Trump told GB News on Thursday that he was not sure if Britain would be prepared to fight for the islands again.
"I just don't know if you have the capacity to do that," Trump said. "The Falklands is very interesting because your country is not the same country it was 20 years ago, 25 years ago."
A potential shift in the U.S. position towards the Falklands was included among a range of options considered by the Pentagon earlier this year to pressure NATO allies it believed failed to support U.S. military operations in the war with Iran.
In 1982, Britain's then-Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher, whom Milei in 2023 described as a "great leader", sent a naval task force to the South Atlantic following an Argentinian invasion. Britain regained control of the islands after 74 days of fighting which left more than 900 people dead.
But in Thursday's address, Milei said Britain was now a country "in decline".
SEA LION OILFIELD
Saying the islands were part of Argentina's future, Milei said he would send Congress an urgent "national sovereignty defence" bill to toughen penalties for unauthorized operations around the islands, extend sanctions to suppliers and broaden the legal framework to cover other activities affecting Argentina's natural resources.
The Sea Lion oilfield, which lies about 140 miles north of the Falkland Islands, is operated by Tel Aviv-listed Navitas Petroleum and also has London-listed Rockhopper Exploration among its shareholders.
In 2010, when drilling first found the field, Argentina said it was illegal. It is estimated to hold 1.7 billion barrels of oil, making it a major discovery in global terms.
Rockhopper stock fell 6% on Friday morning, while Navitas was down 2%. The companies said in a statement they had valid petroleum licences.
"The partnership believes that the recent developments are not expected to have a material effect on the development activities of the Sea Lion Project, including the timetable for completion of the Project's development," they said. REUTERS

Argentinian president vows to toughen sanctions against companies exploiting Falklands oil
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
01:54:44 UTC
10:54:44 KST

Laura Gamba Fadul
04 September 2026•Update: 04 September 2026
Argentine President Javier Milei announced a suite of stringent executive and legislative measures Thursday night aimed at blocking unauthorized offshore oil exploitation in the Falkland Islands (Malvinas), declaring further resource extraction a direct violation of national security.
Surrounded by his full Cabinet during a televised national address, Milei reaffirmed Argentina's territorial claim, asserting that the islands belong to the South American nation "historically and legally."
"The islands have been part of Argentine territory since the origins of our nation," Milei said. "In 1833, the United Kingdom occupied the Falklands, expelled the Argentine authorities, and established a colonial situation that continues to this day." He added that the islanders "do not have a legitimate right to self-determination."
The president pointed specifically to the Sea Lion oil project, operated in the North Falklands Basin by British firm Rockhopper Exploration and Israel-based Navitas Petroleum, as an imminent threat.
"If we do not act firmly and swiftly today, in a few months they will have the capacity to appropriate the oil reserves that lie beneath our sea," Milei warned. "If we allow it, we will create an incentive for the British government to deepen its occupation of our islands and the exploitation of our resources."
To counter the project, Milei signed an executive decree expediting sanctioning procedures against entities involved in unauthorized hydrocarbon operations on Argentina's continental shelf. Under the order, the government will disqualify companies, their shareholders, directors, and commercial suppliers from operating on mainland Argentina.
Milei also announced he will send an urgent bill to Congress to harden existing laws. The proposed legislation would impose identical penalties and bans on third-party service providers and contractors, permanently bar non-compliant entities from public or private sector contracts in Argentina, and authorize trials in absentia for violators.
Milei framed the move around what he described as shifting global diplomatic dynamics, pointing to recent remarks by the US President Donald Trump that Washington is reevaluating its historic position on the Falklands dispute.
"This threat is not innocuous," Milei said. "The United States is evaluating this change in position because they know that in Argentina they have a reliable partner, aligned with Western values, in a strategically important position that could be a valuable ally in the decades to come."
Closing his address, the president called on political opponents to set aside domestic partisan rivalries.
"We can discuss anything else, but this issue demands a pause. It demands that we lay down our weapons and present a united front to the world as a nation," Milei said. "Ensuring our preeminence in this territory is not a political whim. It is a matter of survival."

How the US is taking direct control of Venezuelan oil
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
01:50:00 UTC
10:50:00 KST

How the US is taking direct control of Venezuelan oil
- The US has made a 100-year deal with Venezuela to control 65 billion barrels of oil reserves through North American Blue Energy Partners, with the US government holding significant stakes and rights.
- The deal aims to boost US oil reserves, lower gasoline prices, and strengthen energy independence, while Venezuela expects large investments and economic growth but faces criticism over sovereignty loss.
- Under Trump, the US has increased influence in Venezuela's oil sector by easing sanctions, supporting interim authorities, and encouraging US companies like Chevron to expand operations.
AI generated
NEW YORK – While Venezuela is not the powerhouse oil producer it used to be, the country nonetheless has some of the world’s largest oil reserves.
When the US seized then-Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro on Jan 3, US President Donald Trump was clear that the raid was as much about oil as it was about the narco-terrorism and drug charges levelled against the strongman leader now being held in a federal jail in New York City.
In the months since, the Trump administration has conditioned support for interim President Delcy Rodríguez’s government on a series of measures to open Venezuela’s oil sector to US investors and cede significant control over the industry to the US government.
In late August, the US announced an agreement with Venezuela for the US to take control of more than 65 billion barrels of the nation’s crude reserves. The deal is prompting warnings that the Latin American nation will become a modern-day resource colony akin to the so-called banana republics of a century ago.
Here is what you should know about Venezuela’s oil industry and how the US is seizing access.
How will the US-Venezuela oil deal work
The arrangement gives a private company, North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP), rights to develop a huge swath of Venezuela’s oil reserves, while giving the US government a stake in the company and broad rights to buy its crude.
Here is how it works: Venezuela’s interim authorities have granted NABEP 100-year concessions to operate 17 oil fields with proven reserves of about 65 billion barrels.
NABEP plans to invest as much as US$100 billion (S$127 billion) in new infrastructure and boost production from its operations in the Lake Maracaibo and Orinoco Belt regions.
The Pentagon’s Office of Strategic Capital will take a 35 per cent equity stake in NABEP’s corporate parent, which the White House says could represent hundreds of billions of dollars in value and dividends.
US taxpayers will not finance the venture; NABEP will instead be able to raise private American capital.
The State Department will have the right to buy 20 per cent of the oil produced from NABEP’s current and future fields at the cost of production. The US said the crude could be used to refill the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
The US will also have the first opportunity to buy the remaining 80 per cent of the oil.
Washington will also have veto power over appointments to NABEP’s board, and a majority of NABEP’s members must be US citizens. The agreement will be governed by US law and subject to US courts.
How does the deal benefit the US and Trump?
Trump said the arrangement would more than double US oil reserves and in turn lower petrol prices.
While it will take time to ramp up Venezuelan oil production, the administration is betting that expectations of future supply can help put downward pressure on prices now.
The Trump administration is keen to demonstrate political wins ahead of the midterm elections – the president’s ratings are at a low following the unpopular war in Iran and its impact on affordability.
The potential flows of crude to the US, underpinned by an expected surge in Venezuelan production, will be used to refill the Strategic Petroleum Reserve, according to a White House release. It also stands to boost business for US refineries and oil field-equipment makers.
The deal will likely help the US further secure its energy independence and dominance in world markets. Venezuela’s importance in global oil markets has increased since the outbreak of the Iran war, which has constrained supplies from the Persian Gulf.
Venezuelan oil can reach key markets without passing through some of the world’s most volatile maritime flashpoints, including the Red Sea and the Strait of Hormuz, adding to its appeal.
What does the deal mean for Venezuela?
NABEP’s investment in new oil infrastructure will help drive economic growth and support thousands of jobs in Venezuela.
Over the first quarter century of the 100-year deal, it is expected that NABEP will pay US$200 billion in royalty and tax payments to Venezuela.
Rodriguez cast the agreement as a way to turn Venezuela’s vast underground reserves into “well-being, prosperity and happiness” for its people.
But government loyalists and opposition figures alike criticised the deal, which may strengthen Rodriguez by giving the US a greater stake in her administration’s continuity.
Hard-line supporters of Chavismo, the political movement founded by the late president Hugo Chavez and built in part around state control of Venezuela’s oil, called the deal an abdication of the country’s sovereignty. Some commentators said Venezuela had effectively been forced to give away oil under US threat.
Francisco Rodriguez, a Venezuelan economist and professor at the University of Denver, said Venezuela is “functioning as a protectorate of the US in all but name”.
This arrangement “isn’t furthering the interests of Venezuelans. It’s about securing the economic and security interests of the United States”.
A State Department official rejected the idea that the Trump administration’s efforts in Venezuela were colonial. The move would benefit the country’s people, the person said, while disadvantaging US geopolitical foes Russia and China, whose entities previously controlled some of the fields to be operated by NABEP.
How much oil does Venezuela have?
The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) estimates Venezuela sits atop nearly 304 billion barrels of oil, or the equivalent of 20 per cent of the world’s crude reserves – more than Saudi Arabia.
But some analysts claim the real number is about a third of that, or around 100 billion barrels. While the figure may not be as colossal as OPEC’s estimate, it is still nearly double the combined reserves of the US, Canada, Mexico and Chile.
Venezuela currently produces around a million barrels a day, less than 1 per cent of global output. Oil production will take decades to return to its 1990s peak of more than three million barrels a day, even as a deal with the US prompts a boost in near-term output, according to Rystad Energy.
Despite the sector’s decline, at least 95 per cent of Venezuela’s overseas revenue comes from oil sales.
Under the US deal, NABEP said it plans to boost production from its operations in Venezuela’s Lake Maracaibo and Orinoco Belt to more than 1 million barrels of oil per day.
Under Trump, what role has the US taken in Venezuela’s oil industry?
Trump has described Venezuela as the 51st state and said the US will “rebuild” the country’s underproducing oil industry.
In January, Trump appeared to threaten Rodríguez’s life if she did not comply with the US’ priorities.
“If she doesn’t do what’s right, she is going to pay a very big price, probably bigger than Maduro,” he said in an interview with the Atlantic.
Under US pressure, Rodríguez has succeeded in enacting new hydrocarbons and mining laws that favor investors and ditch decades of tight state controls.
The US Treasury is easing sanctions on the state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela, or PDV, and expanding licenses for more US and international firms to do business with the state-owned company.
Washington has kept close oversight of the process while controlling the country’s oil revenues, which it is holding in US Treasury accounts.
It had allowed around US$3 billion to flow into the economy as at mid-April and has promised that independent audits run by professional services firm KPMG will be published. It’s unclear when the reports from the auditing firms will be released.
Crude and gas production has not significantly ramped up yet.
While most oil majors have left the country in recent years, a handful have held on, including Chevron – the only American company still operating in the country – Italy’s Eni and Spain’s Repsol.
Trump’s efforts to attract producers to return to the country yielded no new investments for the first seven months after Maduro’s ouster.
But in early September, Chevron finalised a deal that will significantly expand its operations in Venezuela by adding two giant oil fields in the Orinoco Belt territory. Chevron accounts for about a quarter of Venezuelan oil production. Other deals with US companies are expected to follow.
In a sign of the US’s deepening role in Venezuela’s oil industry, Venezuela is considering whether it should quit OPEC, which it helped found in 1960, according to people familiar with the matter, and is discussing the possibility with US officials.
What has been the role of US oil companies in Venezuela?
US oil companies were the main architects of Venezuela’s oil industry starting a century ago, building the country into a leading US supplier.
The industry was nationalised in the mid-1970s and reopened to foreign investment in the 1990s.
Chavez, Maduro’s predecessor, expropriated major US oil projects in 2007.
Exxon Mobil and ConocoPhillips pulled out and later won sweeping international arbitration awards for the seizure of their assets. BLOOMBERG

SAN FRANCISCO, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- U.S. chipmaker Nvidia has agreed to acquire artificial intelligence (AI) developer platform Hugging Face for about 12.93 billion U.S. dollars, Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang announced Thursday.
Huang said in a company blog post that the two companies will work together to scale Hugging Face's platform, strengthen its infrastructure and expand access to AI for developers and institutions worldwide.
Hugging Face will remain an open platform for the entire AI ecosystem, Huang said.
"NVIDIA compute will not be required to build on or deploy through Hugging Face," Huang noted.
He added that Hugging Face will continue to support open-source and open-weight models from different model developers, as well as multi-cloud and multi-accelerator development and deployment.
According to Huang, more than 18 million developers, researchers and creators use Hugging Face, where they share more than 3 million models, 500,000 datasets and 1 million applications. More than 200,000 companies use the platform to discover, evaluate, customize and deploy AI.
Huang said Nvidia's infrastructure, engineering capabilities and global reach could help improve Hugging Face's platform reliability, safety, model evaluation, inference and deployment capabilities while preserving its open ecosystem.
Nvidia has also been expanding its involvement in open AI models. Huang said the company has released more than 500 models and more than 250 open datasets on Hugging Face, describing Nvidia as the platform's largest contributor of open models and data.
Hugging Face was founded by Clement Delangue, Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf. ■

by sportswriter Dong Yixing
BEIJING, Sept. 4 (Xinhua) -- Song Yadong didn't sleep at all on the night of August 29, after registering the most significant victory of his UFC career so far.
"I was too excited to sleep. The excitement still hasn't fully worn off. Every time I open my phone, it's all about me," Song told Xinhua on Thursday.
In the main event at UFC Fight Night Shanghai at the Oriental Sports Center, Song knocked out Russia's Umar Nurmagomedov in the second round with a devastating uppercut, putting himself into the bantamweight title conversation.
The 28-year-old Chinese spent the night at a post-fight party with friends and celebrities who had traveled there from around the world. Congratulatory messages kept pouring in, and he didn't finish replying until five days later.
Few expected Song to win. Nurmagomedov, cousin of former lightweight champion Khabib Nurmagomedov, entered the bout ranked third in the division with a professional record of 20-1 and a formidable grappling pedigree. Song, meanwhile, had come up short in three previous high-profile fights against Petr Yan, Sean O'Malley and Cory Sandhagen.
But Song's boxing coach Rudy Hernandez had predicted the finish. "He told me I would knock him out with an uppercut. I thought, how can he be so confident? My opponent is very strong, and nobody was picking me to win," Song recalled.
"But I believed in him. That's why I brought him over from the United States. If I didn't trust him, there would have been no point."
The fight played out exactly as rehearsed. Nurmagomedov took Song down early and controlled him on the ground for much of the first round, but Song remained calm.
"I knew he would take me down. I had visualized that moment countless times in my head, so I wasn't nervous at all. I was only thinking about how to get back up," he said.
In the second round, Song reacted on instinct. "My goal was to use the uppercut. When he came in, I was attacking at the same time, and my body just threw the punch naturally."
The fight was over at 1:48 of round two. Song's post-fight assessment of his opponent was simple: "The only thing that changed is that I actually overestimated him."
Song's composure under pressure didn't come naturally. For years, he struggled with the weight of expectations, particularly in big fights. The turning point came after his loss to O'Malley, when his coach recommended a mental performance coach based in Canada.
The two worked together online for about 10 sessions. When asked why he fought, Song answered because of love and responsibility. The mental performance coach's response changed everything.
"He said responsibility should be deleted, because responsibility won't make you perform better. Only love can do that," Song said. "He asked me when I was happiest, and told me to write down those moments and practice them."
Before the Nurmagomedov fight, Song's mental performance coach introduced visualization and meditation techniques. For six weeks, Song spent 15 minutes every day mentally rehearsing every detail of fight night - the music during his walkout, the feel of hand wraps, the roar of the crowd, the smell of the gloves, even the taste of blood.
"By the time it actually happened, nothing surprised me. I had already lived through it a thousand times," Song explained.
The results were visible. Cameras caught Song smiling after the first round, even as Nurmagomedov controlled him on the ground. An American MMA journalist later asked him why he was smiling against such a dangerous opponent.
After the fight, Song sent a message to Nurmagomedov, expressing respect for him and his team. "I told him that outside the octagon, we are friends. Inside the octagon, we go all out. He replied that he felt the same way, but that he would come back for a rematch."
Song, however, has his eyes on a different target. "I'd really like to fight Merab Dvalishvili. Let's see who wins between him and Yan, and then maybe their next fight. I'm hoping for early next year."
As for the growing expectation that he could become China's first male UFC champion, Song insists the pressure no longer weighs on him. "I've already passed that stage. I've fought many tough battles, and my mentality is in the best place it's ever been. I can face any opponent right now."
Song made his UFC debut in Shanghai in 2017. Nine years later, he returned to the same city and delivered the performance of his life. Reflecting on his journey, he said the biggest change has been mental.
"Life is about cultivating the mind. When you're young, everything is new, and you don't know how to handle it. You can be impatient, afraid, or want to give up. But through all these experiences, you grow stronger and calmer inside. Technique can be trained, but mentality is not so easy to change."
What hasn't changed, he said, is his upward drive and his love for the sport. "Too many people change their dreams and goals every year because they think the path is too hard. They end up achieving nothing. I never changed."
For now, Song plans to finish his media and commercial obligations, take a short rest, and return to training by the end of the month. The win itself, he said, is the greatest reward he could ask for.
"I don't need fancy cars or expensive watches or vacations. This is the biggest gift I could give myself - proving my ability, becoming more confident, and performing better than ever." ■

Breaking: Bathla creditors' meeting hears company owes $3.4 billion
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
01:42:05 UTC
10:42:05 KST

Bathla Group reveals $3.4b debt as administrators warn some work could halt
At Bathla's first creditors' meeting, administrator Teneo said it was in "positive discussions" with five lenders over funding to keep construction going, with Monday morning the key deadline.
Teneo senior managing director Stephen Longley said in the virtual call that he hoped to have the funding arrangements in place by the end of today, but they were giving themselves until Monday morning.
If the five lenders provide funding, construction on their sites can continue, but administrators say they "probably won't be able to support" construction on sites whose lenders are not participating.
Administrators estimate supporting construction would cost the business about $1 million to $1.3 million a week, depending on which projects continue.
Bathla is one of Sydney's biggest residential property developers, with a large pipeline of housing projects and land holdings across the region.
The group was placed into voluntary administration last week after running into severe cashflow problems, leaving administrators to work out which projects can keep operating and how creditors will be repaid.
Much of Bathla's development activity is financed project by project through separate lenders, which has made it difficult to find a single funding solution for the broader business.
Company's debt and property position revealed
Bathla Group owes known creditors about $3.4 billion, based on preliminary figures.
The vast majority ($3.08 billion) is owed to secured lenders.
Bathla also owes about $145 million to the Australian Taxation Office, $42 million in land tax and $130 million to other unsecured creditors.
About $4 million is owed to employees for wages and superannuation.
Administrators also put the preliminary stated value of Bathla's 219 sites at about $4.9 billion.
But Teneo has said the $4.9 billion is not cash available to pay creditors. Much of that value is tied up in land and developments, which can take time to sell, and the valuations are preliminary and still being checked.
Much of Bathla's property is also financed by individual lenders. That means proceeds from a property sale will likely need to go towards that project or its lender, rather than being available to fund the broader Bathla business.
Administrators also said that about $400 million worth of property was currently for sale or under contract, but no cash from that was expected to flow to the group in the near term.
Customer deposits
There were also a number of questions from people attending the meeting about the status of customer deposits.
Administrators said they were still carrying out a full reconciliation, with deposits spread across trust accounts held by multiple law firms.
They confirmed not all customer deposits were sitting in trust accounts, because some sale contracts allowed part of the deposit to be used by the business to fund projects.
However, administrators said some contracts had still settled this week even where the deposits were not held in trust.

Missouri statehouse candidate accused of trying to plant drugs on opponent
Sept 3 - The Republican nominee for a Missouri statehouse seat has been charged in federal court with conspiracy to distribute narcotics, accused of plotting to plant drugs on his primary election rival in the final months of the race.
Thomas Christopher Ross, 37, who won the Republican primary for the 161st district of the Missouri House of Representatives by a mere 33 votes in August, was charged in a single-count criminal complaint filed by federal prosecutors on Wednesday.
The case was announced on Thursday by the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Missouri.
According to prosecutors, Ross spent weeks hatching a plan with his campaign manager to frame his opponent, Louise Secker, by surreptitiously placing a black nylon glove containing a bag of cocaine and a capsule of the prescription stimulant Adderall into her car or purse.
Under the alleged scheme, outlined in a seven-page FBI affidavit, the campaign manager would then alert law enforcement through "an anonymous tip" that Secker had drugs in her possession.
The plot, which apparently was never carried out, was to be acted on while Ross was away on vacation in South Carolina in June 2026, according to the affidavit.
The affidavit said Ross and the campaign manager, who was not named in court documents, communicated through text messages in coded language, including one in which Ross referred to the desired outcome as "extreme egg on the face" of his opponent.
According to the affidavit, the investigation began when the campaign manager alerted police in Joplin, Missouri, who turned the case over to the FBI. The campaign aide provided the bag containing the drugs that he said Ross wanted planted on Secker, as well as texts he had shared with his boss.
Neither Ross nor either of the two attorneys in the public defender's office assigned to his case could immediately be reached for comment.
The chairman of the Missouri Republican Party, Peter Kinder, issued a statement on Wednesday calling on Ross to immediately resign as the party's nominee for the House seat.
"While Mr. Ross is entitled to due process and the facts surrounding this matter must be allowed to come to light, the circumstances of his arrest are serious and deeply troubling," Kinder wrote.
There was no immediate response from Secker or her campaign.
If convicted, Ross could face a sentence of up to 20 years in prison. REUTERS

Kyiv traffic to halt during nationwide minute of silence
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
01:29:00 UTC
10:29:00 KST

Kyiv traffic to halt during nationwide minute of silence
This was announced by the Kyiv City State Administration; the Kyiv City Council supported the decision, according to Ukrinform.
“Every day at 9:00 a.m., during the nationwide minute of silence, traffic in Kyiv will be halted for 60 seconds. Where technically possible, traffic lights will be switched to ‘all red,’” the statement reads.
The draft resolution was developed pursuant to a protocol directive from Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko in response to a request from Kyiv City Council members who are currently serving in the Armed Forces of Ukraine.
It is noted that transportation experts analyzed various scenarios for halting traffic during the minute of silence, conducted the necessary simulations, and determined a mechanism that will allow this to be done in a controlled and safe manner, without unduly disrupting transportation operations. This decision is intended to demonstrate that even in a large city, remembrance need not be a mere formality but rather a collective act, and that Kyiv is capable of pausing at a crucial moment, behaving with dignity, and setting an example.
As explained by Kostiantyn Usov, Deputy Head of the Kyiv City State Administration for the Exercise of Self-Government Powers and a member of the Kyiv City Council, this decision is intended to make the minute of silence in the capital truly visible and turn it into a daily tradition of remembrance.
He added that the city must keep moving. People must go to work, to school, and about their business. Kyiv cannot bring life to a standstill. But once a day, Kyiv can pause for one minute and remember the price at which this life continues.
“We cannot bring back those who have fallen in battle. But we can ensure that their sacrifice does not fade into the background. That it does not get lost in the city’s noise. So that in the capital of Ukraine, remembrance is visible, tangible, and shared. This is a simple yet very important urban standard of respect. And respect for those who have fallen in Kyiv will not be mere words. It will take shape, action, order, and daily consistency,” Usov emphasized.
In the first phase, traffic will be halted in the central part of the capital, where the system is already technically ready: on European Square, Khreshchatyk Street, Baseina Street, Bessarabsky Passage, Velyka Vasylkivska Street, Ukrainian Heroes Square, Yevhen Chykalenko Street, Taras Shevchenko Boulevard, Volodymyrska Street, and Prorizna Street.
In the future, as traffic signal systems become technically ready, this measure will be extended to other streets and areas of Kyiv.
During traffic stops, the city’s public address system will broadcast a voice announcement and a countdown until the end of the minute of silence.
The mechanism will take the security situation into account: traffic will not be halted for 60 seconds while an “air raid alert” signal is active or being announced.
Public and private ground public transportation operators will be informed of the new procedure. The date on which traffic in the capital will begin to be halted during the nationwide minute of silence will be announced separately.
As reported by Ukrinform, the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine passed a law honoring the memory of Ukrainians who died as a result of the Russian Federation’s armed aggression. The nationwide minute of silence is to be observed daily at 9:00 a.m.

Of the 32 "Rassvet" satellites, only 12 reached a stable operational altitude. At the same time, the developers announced that service testing had started ahead of schedule.
The Russian company "Bureau 1440," which is creating the low-orbit satellite constellation "Rassvet" as an analogue of Starlink, said it was ahead of schedule amid reports of problems with the launched spacecraft. The Moscow Times reports this, writes UNN.
Details
Oleksii Shelobkov, head of "X Holding," said that all technological risks of the project remained "manageable and predictable." According to him, the company had already moved to internal testing and user trials in August, although this stage was initially planned for September.

According to the Institute for the Study of War, none of the 16 spacecraft launched on July 19 managed to reach the planned altitude of 870 km. Only 37.5% of the satellites reached their operational altitude

According to the ISW's assessment, only 37.5% of the launched "Rassvet" spacecraft had reached a stable operational altitude overall.
At the same time, Shelobkov said that key users had already been given the opportunity to test the service. According to him, the first "Rassvet" terminal was installed on rolling stock belonging to Russian Railways, and its testing is expected to begin shortly.
Russia is developing "Rassvet" as its own alternative to Starlink. The ISW believes that problems with the second batch of satellites may indicate Russia's lack of readiness to deploy the constellation at the planned pace and could lead to additional delays.

Russia’s bid for closer defense, economic, and nuclear relations with Indonesia is a clear attempt to strengthen its influence in the Global South and reduce the effectiveness of Western efforts to isolate the country since its invasion of Ukraine in early 2022. For Indonesia, a closer relationship with Russia is an important component of Prabowo’s policy of assertive non-alignment, which seeks improved relations with nations of all geopolitical persuasions.

What is celebrated on September 4 in Ukraine and around the world
Ukraine
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
04:08:10 EEST
10:08:10 KST

What is celebrated on September 4 in Ukraine and around the world
Kyiv • UNN
On September 4, Ukraine commemorates the raising of the blue-and-yellow flag over the Verkhovna Rada in 1991. Around the world, Sexual Health Day and Taekwondo Day are observed.
On September 4, people commemorate the raising of the blue-and-yellow flag over the Verkhovna Rada of Ukraine in 1991, mark World Sexual Health Day and World Taekwondo Day, and also remember the Prophet Moses and the icon "The Unburnt Bush" according to the new church calendar, reports UNN.
Raising of the State Flag of Ukraine over the Verkhovna Rada
An event of historic significance for Ukrainian state-building: on September 4, 1991, at the insistence of members of parliament and after lengthy debates, the national blue-and-yellow flag was officially raised for the first time over the parliament building alongside the flag of the Ukrainian SSR. This became a symbolic step toward affirming sovereignty and preceded the Verkhovna Rada’s resolution granting official status to the blue-and-yellow flag in January 1992.
World Sexual Health Day
An inaugural day established in 2010 by the World Association for Sexual Health (WAS) to promote sexual rights, sex education, and disease prevention. The initiative emphasizes that sexual health is an integral part of a person’s overall physical and psychological well-being, as well as the right to safety and personal integrity.
World Taekwondo Day
The date commemorates the decision of the International Olympic Committee on September 4, 1994, at its session in Paris, to include the Korean martial art of taekwondo in the official program of the Olympic Games. The holiday brings together millions of athletes around the world and promotes the philosophy of discipline, self-control, and respect.
International Newspaper Carrier Day
The event originated as a commemoration of Barney Flaherty—the world’s first teenager hired to work as a newspaper seller and carrier by the publisher of The New York Sun in 1833. The day is dedicated to recognizing the importance of the work of print-media distributors and the development of journalism.
Memorial Day of the Holy Prophet Moses the Seer of God
According to the new calendar, believers commemorate the Holy Prophet Moses the Seer of God, who led the people of Israel out of Egyptian captivity and received the Ten Commandments on Mount Sinai, as well as Hieromartyr Babylas, Bishop of Great Antioch, who was executed in the 3rd century for refusing to let a pagan emperor into the church. The day of the icon of the Mother of God "The Unburnt Bush" is also observed; the icon is considered the patroness of firefighters and a protector against fires.
According to the old calendar, the Orthodox Church commemorates the holy martyr Agathonicus of Nicomedia and others who were executed with him during the reign of Emperor Maximian for refusing to renounce the Christian faith. In the folk calendar, this day was called "Agathon the Haystack Guardian" and was associated with beliefs about protecting sheaves and threshing floors from forest spirits, which is why peasants traditionally kept watch over their grain at night.

Last EC-130H Makes Its Final Flight Ahead of Retirement
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
01:06:07 UTC
10:06:07 KST

The last EC-130H Compass Call in the Air Force’s active inventory made its final flight Sept. 2, as the service prepares to retire the venerable electronic warfare aircraft and pivot to the new EA-37B.
A spokesperson for the 55th Wing confirmed the event, often called a “fini flight,” to Air & Space Forces Magazine. A formal retirement ceremony for the aircraft will take place Sept. 18 at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base, Ariz., where the last flight also took place.
Aviation photographer Steven Fortson snapped images of the final flight, including photos of an EA-37 in the air at the same time.
The end has been a long time coming for the EC-130H—the Air Force first announced plans to retire the EC-130 in 2014 and finally awarded a contract to what was then L3 Technologies to move critical mission systems from the aircraft to new business jets in 2017. The first of the Compass Calls retired in 2021, and the Air Force has slowly culled the 14-aircraft in the years since.
At the same time, the aircraft and its crews have stayed extremely busy given the demand for electronic warfare capabilities. First converted from the workhorse C-130 Hercules in the early 1980s, the type can target, block, and jam enemy communications, radar, or navigation signals.
Aircraft spotters noted one landing in the Caribbean last December, days before Operation Absolute Resolve, the high-stakes raid on Caracas, Venezuela, to snatch and grab Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro. And U.S. Central Command confirmed early this year it used the EC-130H in the early days of Operation Epic Fury, the air campaign against Iran.
Indeed, the EC-130 has been a fixture in operations for more than 35 years. It saw its combat debut during Operations Just Cause in Panama in 1989, then flew in Operation Desert Storm in 1991, Operation Allied Force in Kosovo in 1999, and throughout the Global War on Terror over Afghanistan, Iraq, and Syria during the 2000s.
Now, much of its mission is transferring to the EA-37B, a modified Gulfstream 550 that will include about 70 percent of the EC-130’s EW systems unchanged. The EA-37B carries a combat crew of nine people, down from 13 on the EC-130H.
The first EA-37 arrived at Davis-Monthan in August 2024, and the jets deployed to support Operation Epic Fury in late March, making their combat debut before the EA-37 had even been formally declared operational. More deployed to the United Kingdom in July, as hostilities with Iran persisted.
Right now, the Air Force has only five EA-37s of the 10 aircraft it has ordered. But the service has plans to expand the fleet to 22 airframes with procurement continuing through 2031. Officials say the expanded fleet—even bigger than the original EC-130H fleet—is necessary given the importance of electronic warfare in modern combat and the demand from combatant commanders.
Pentagon Editor Chris Gordon contributed to this report.

Unknown

In short:
Alex de Minaur was beaten 6-4, 7-5, 6-2 by Dutch world number 70 Botic van de Zandschulp.
The victory was van de Zandschulp's first over de Minaur in five attempts.
What's next?
Wildcard Dane Sweeny is the only Australian left in the men's singles draw at Flushing Meadows
Alex de Minaur has been dumped out of the US Open in the second round, falling in straight sets to Dutchman Botic van de Zandschulp 6-4, 7-5, 6-2 in two hours and 43 minutes.
De Minaur had never lost to the 30-year-old world number 70 in their previous four meetings, including earlier this year at the Rotterdam ATP event, which the 27-year-old Aussie won.
But on a night where he committed 29 unforced errors to van de Zandschulp's 21, as well as seven double faults in a sub-par serving display, the Australian world number seven faltered badly.
"I always had really difficult matches against Alex," van de Zandschulp said on court.
"Some tough ones as well, some close matches, but today I served very well, I think that was the difference today."
De Minaur saved three match points in the final game, but it was not enough, the Aussie leaving himself far too much to do.
After a brief pause where he stood on court in contemplation at his exit, de Minaur exited without looking back.
The defeat is de Minaur's earliest exit at the US Open in five years, at a slam where he has three times reached the quarterfinals.
With Novak Djokovic and Félix Auger-Aliassime both crashing out, de Minaur had been the fourth-highest seed left in the tournament.
But he was unable to make that opportunity count.
De Minaur was forced to wait until day four to get his tournament underway after rain caused the postponement of his round one clash with Italian qualifier Andrea Guerrieri.
The victory is van de Zandschulp's second over a top-10 player during this US hardcourt swing after he beat world number eight Daniil Medvedev at the Montreal Masters in August.
The one-time US Open quarterfinalist has made a habit of pulling off shock victories at Flushing Meadows.
He beat Casper Ruud on his way to the quarterfinal in 2021 and, in 2024, knocked out third-seed Carlos Alcaraz in the second round with a straight-sets win.
De Minaur's exit means wildcard Dane Sweeny is the only Australian left in the men's singles draw at Flushing Meadows after his 3-6, 6-1, 6-2, 6-2 victory against world number 14 Lorenzo Musetti.

Notorious Israeli minister and far-right Jewish Power party leader Itamar Ben-Gvir has presented an ethnic cleansing plan to expel 1.86 million Palestinians from besieged Gaza in seven years under "voluntary migration," according to Israeli media.
Ben-Gvir presented the scheme, called "Disengagement 710," at a news conference on Thursday as part of his election campaign after the Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper published details of the initiative.
The plan includes establishing a special ministry to implement the project and fund "absorption packages" in receiving countries, said the daily.
During the presentation, Ben-Gvir claimed there are countries "ready to receive" Palestinians and that "large numbers want to move."
But Yedioth Ahronoth said no country is currently known to have agreed to accept large numbers of Palestinians from Gaza.
The plan targets expelling 250,000 Palestinians in the first year, 1.11 million within three years and about 1.86 million within seven years, said the report.
Ben-Gvir plans to make the initiative a central part of his election campaign after "working on it for months," it added.
His Jewish Power party also plans to make adoption of the initiative a key demand in any negotiations to join the next government, said Yedioth Ahronoth.
It includes providing a destination country for each individual or family leaving Gaza along with legal status, documentation, visas, travel funding and initial housing.
'Migration ministry'
The plan is based on 12 principles, including what it calls "voluntary departure" and a requirement that "no one leave without a country prepared to receive them and provide them with regulated legal status," according to the report.
The plan also proposes "payments" to countries and entities involved in receiving those leaving Gaza based on "their performance, individual security screening and annual implementation targets."
It calls for "monthly reports on the number of applications, approvals and departures" as well as "costs and the extent to which those leaving are integrated into their destination countries."
The plan would require an initial Israeli investment of $3.3 billion for it to be established and launched.
It also envisages an Israeli financing framework of up to $16.6 billion subject to international participation and agreements with destination countries.
Ben-Gvir demanded the establishment of a "migration ministry," saying it would have a minister and a special official in charge of the project.
Around 2.13 million Palestinians currently live in besieged Gaza.
Israel, which occupies 70 percent of Gaza, has killed over 73,000 Palestinians, mostly women and children, and wounded more than 174,000 others in its genocide in Gaza since October 2023.
It reduced most of the blockade enclave to ruins and displaced its entire population.
Analysts estimate the actual death toll from Israel's genocide in Gaza may be significantly higher than official figures, potentially reaching 200,000.

Deep beneath Mars, scientists find a vast hidden magma system
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-04
00:52:29 UTC
09:52:29 KST

Deep beneath Mars, scientists find a vast hidden magma system
- Date:
- September 3, 2026
- Source:
- University of Oxford
- Summary:
- Deep beneath Mars, scientists have found evidence of enormous magmatic systems once thought to require Earth-like plate tectonics. Seismic measurements suggest molten rock repeatedly evolved and recycled itself through the Martian crust, potentially across hundreds or thousands of kilometers. The discovery challenges long-held ideas about how complex planetary crusts form.
- Share:
Researchers at the University of Oxford have found evidence that Mars may once have contained enormous Earth-like magmatic systems deep below its surface, even though the planet does not have the plate tectonics that scientists have long associated with this level of geological complexity. The findings, published in Nature Astronomy, point to new possibilities for how rocky planets can evolve in ways that may support habitability.
Mars is commonly classified as a "stagnant lid" planet because, unlike Earth, its outer shell is not divided into moving tectonic plates. On Earth, plate tectonics plays a major role in volcanism, recycling crustal material and helping build continents. Because Mars lacks this process, scientists have often assumed that its crust formed in a much simpler way.
The new study challenges that assumption. The results suggest that Mars may have developed highly evolved crust through vigorous recycling within the planet itself, without the need for Earth-style plate tectonics.
A Mysterious Boundary 24 Kilometers Down
The researchers analyzed seismic data collected by NASA's InSight mission, focusing on waves generated by meteoroid impacts and marsquakes, the Martian equivalent of earthquakes.
Scientists from Oxford's Departments of Earth Sciences and Statistics used those measurements to study an unexplained boundary roughly 24 kilometers beneath the Martian surface. Earlier research had identified the boundary, but its meaning remained unclear.
To investigate whether it represented a transition between different kinds of rock, the team compared the seismic observations with hundreds of possible rock compositions. They combined thermodynamic modeling with statistical methods to determine which materials best matched the properties detected at different depths.
The analysis showed that rocks beneath the 24 km boundary were best explained by "ultramafic" material (rich in iron and magnesium, but low in silica). Above the boundary, the seismic properties were more consistent with "mafic" rocks (containing a higher proportion of silica).
Evidence of a Vast Magma System
The researchers think the buried layer formed when molten rock accumulated deep underground and gradually separated into different materials. In this process, dense crystals would have settled near the bottom of the crust, while lighter and more chemically evolved melts moved upward.
On Earth, similar processes occur beneath volcanic arcs and are associated with the formation of continents.
Lead author Dr. Tobermory Mackay-Champion (Department of Earth Sciences, University of Oxford at the time of the study, now University of Bristol) said: "We've traditionally assumed that volcanism on Mars was relatively simple compared to that on Earth. But this discovery suggests Mars could sustain large, long-lived systems where molten rock evolved and reprocessed itself throughout the entire crust. It raises exciting possibilities for how common such systems might be on rocky planets beyond our solar system."
The buried layer may also be enormous in scale. According to the study, it could extend for hundreds or even thousands of kilometers across Mars' northern hemisphere.
That would suggest ancient Mars was not dominated only by simple, isolated volcanoes. Instead, the planet may once have contained huge, connected magmatic systems spanning large portions of its crust.
This process, known as "transcrustal magmatism," had previously been thought to be unique to Earth.
What This Could Mean for Habitable Planets
The findings could have broader implications for understanding how rocky planets become habitable.
Geological recycling can influence the development of atmospheres, oceans and environments where life might be possible. On Earth, these processes help regulate climate and support the long-term cycling of water and other volatile elements.
Because plate tectonics drives much of that recycling on Earth, scientists have often viewed it as an important requirement for creating and maintaining habitable conditions. The Mars findings suggest that complex crustal evolution and extensive geological recycling may be possible even on planets without Earth-style tectonics.
Co-author Professor Jon Wade (Department of Earth Sciences, University of Oxford) said: "One of the big questions in planetary science is whether Earth is unique. If Mars could develop this kind of complex crust without plate tectonics, then maybe the conditions needed for habitability can emerge on more planets than we realized, including those previously dismissed based on size or their apparent lack of tectonic activity."
InSight Reveals Mars' Hidden Interior
The research builds on seismic observations collected by NASA's InSight mission, which placed the first seismometer on Mars in 2018 and gave scientists an unprecedented view of the planet's internal structure.
The study was led by researchers from Oxford University's Department of Earth Sciences in collaboration with the University of Bristol and the University of Oxford's Department of Statistics.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Oxford. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- T. Mackay-Champion, M. Anderson Loake, R. Palin, J. Wade, J.-M. Kendall. Seismic evidence for a melt-depleted lower crust and transcrustal magmatism on Mars. Nature Astronomy, 2026; DOI: 10.1038/s41550-026-02907-5
